label: CJEU C-311/18 — Data Protection Commissioner v Facebook Ireland (Schrems II)
body: 1. The GDPR applies to a commercial transfer of personal data to a third country, irrespective of whether that data is liable to be processed there by public authorities for national-security purposes.

2. Art. 46 SCCs require that subjects be afforded a level of protection "essentially equivalent" to that guaranteed within the EU by the GDPR read with the Charter. Assessment must take into account both the SCCs themselves AND any access by third-country public authorities to the data transferred.

3. Where SCCs cannot be complied with in the third country and protection cannot be ensured by other means, the competent SA is required to suspend or prohibit the transfer if the controller/processor hasn't done so itself.
4. The 2010/87 SCCs are valid in principle.

5. Commission Implementing Decision 2016/1250 (EU-US Privacy Shield) is invalid: US surveillance under FISA §702 and EO 12333 fails the essentially-equivalent test; there are no actionable redress rights for EU subjects.
Why it matters: Killed Privacy Shield and made the TIA (transfer impact assessment) mandatory. Drove the 2021 SCC modernisation. Schrems III pending on the DPF.
